title.narrative: Building Resilience through Agroecology for Coastal Emergencies in Bangladesh - BRACE

description.narrative:
Caritas Bangladesh and CAFOD have been working on agroecology for many years, including since 2019 in the coastal region of Barishal, where Caritas Bangladesh, with funding from CAFOD, have been implementing the Proyash project, which focuses on promoting agroecology practices to strengthen resilience and improve livelihoods of the poorest and most marginalized. In May 2024, cyclone Remal hit the southern coastal belt of Bangladesh having a significant impact on the lives of thousands of people, including a large number of the project participants from the Proyash project.
Caritas Bangladesh has undertaken a number of initial assessments of the impacted area, including the impact on the lives and livelihoods of the Proyash participants. Although the assessment has shown the cyclone had a significant impact on the lives of Proyash participants, the initial findings suggest that the Proyash participants are better off and have been able to adapt and recover more quickly from the cyclone than neighbouring community members who were not practicing agroecology practices prior to the cyclone. Initial analysis suggests this is due to a number of factors including better preparedness initiatives such as moving plants/saplings above ground, raising livestock housing, protecting compost sheds as well as post cyclone agroecology initiatives such as using local seed banks to replant lost crops, starting to sell and use vermi compost (organic) again to increase family income after the cyclone.
This study that will be done by BOKU university will aim to demonstrate more clearly the role of agroecology in mitigating the impact of the cyclone and highlight how agroecology techniques can help to strengthen resilience to climate change impacts and natural disasters.
